content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the structure of alcohols and identify the hydroxyl group
Name and draw alcohols with up to 4 carbon atoms
Describe the physical properties of alcohols
Describe how ethanol is made by fermentation and hydration

are organic compounds containing the hydroxyl functional group (-OH). The most well-known alcohol is ethanol, found in alcoholic drinks. Alcohols have many important uses as solvents, fuels, and in chemical synthesis.
Consists of oxygen bonded to hydrogen
Oxygen also bonds to a carbon atom
The -OH group determines the properties of alcohols
Makes alcohols polar and soluble in water
[DIAGRAM: Displayed formula of ethanol showing all bonds]
-OH group forms hydrogen bonds with water
Larger hydrocarbon chain is less soluble
The O-H bond is polar (O is more electronegative)
The δ+ hydrogen can attract δ- oxygen of another molecule

Write the equation for the fermentation of glucose.
Explain why ethanol has a higher boiling point than ethane.
Ethanol molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other
These hydrogen bonds are stronger than the van der Waals forces between ethane molecules
More energy is needed to overcome hydrogen bonds
Therefore, ethanol has a higher boiling point (78°C vs -89°C)
Compare fermentation and hydration as methods for making ethanol.
Writing alcohols as C₂H₅HO instead of C₂H₅OH
The -OH group stays together as hydroxyl
Methanol (CH₃OH) is toxic; ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is in drinks
Higher boiling points due to hydrogen bonding; small alcohols soluble in water
